analysis.title: The Flow Show: When AI met ABB
key_insights: YTD total returns as of 10/28/2026: oil 79.1%, US stocks 12.7%, global stocks 9.6%, US$ 3.7%, cash 3.1%, HY bonds -0.5%, IG -2.5%, govt bonds -3.3%, gold -7.1%, bitcoin -8.4%.

BofA counts 42 global central bank hikes over the past six months. Over the past four months the US$ and UST yields rose and tech leadership stalled or reversed (NDX capped near 30k, SOX -20%). BofA calls this classic painful tightening that is not mortal unless there are job losses or a credit event.
The next big risk-on allocation move awaits the end of hikes and a collapse in oil in H1'27. BofA's levels to hold before a year-end rally are MAGS $70 (Mag7) and SMH $520 (semis).

Polymarket odds of a Democratic midterm sweep are rising and BofA says a risk-off sweep is getting priced in. A Democratic wave (+53 Senate seats) and a jump in bond yields are not priced. Voters want 'affordability', which BofA reads as negative for tech, bank and energy monopolies in '27 and positive for consumer discretionary.

China: new low bond yields, CNY up more than 20% vs the Taiwan dollar over the past year, China tech (CQQQ) -32% since June, China financials 2x over three years. BofA is short oil in H1'27 as peace boosts supply. If lower oil does not trigger a Euro and Yen bounce, that would signal China deflation is a new global negative.

BofA recommends buying tech bonds as 'diamonds in the rough'. US tech bonds are -9% YTD and their return relative to the IG bond index is at a 30-year low. AI hyperscaler debt issuance is $182bn in '26 vs $17bn in '24. Mag7 bond yields of 6-8% are described as attractive.

Hyperscaler equity issuance is $89bn in '26, which BofA reads as the end of the big buyback era. Buybacks run at $14bn YTD annualized vs $105bn in '24. META equity issuance signals new respect for credit investors.
Weekly flows (EPFR, week to 10/28): $56.2bn to stocks, $15.4bn to bonds, $3.4bn to cash, $0.5bn out of crypto, $1.7bn out of gold. Gold's outflow is the first since Jul'26.

Regional flows: China +$25.7bn (biggest since Apr'25, 'national team' buying), Japan +$6.8bn (biggest inflow since May'13), Europe -$2.3bn (biggest outflow since Jul'26). Tech +$5.3bn (5th week of inflows), materials -$1.2bn.

BofA private clients ($4.6tn AUM) hold 66.0% stocks, 17.5% bonds and 9.4% cash. Their weekly equity inflow was the 2nd highest ever, driven by IPO proceeds. They bought municipal, industrials and healthcare ETFs and sold staples, EM debt and consumer discretionary ETFs.
The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator is 7.1 (Neutral), down from 7.2. Weaker global stock index breadth and wider HY and subordinated bank spreads were partly offset by strong equity inflows.

BofA sees four 2020s super trends: ABB (Anything but Bonds), ABC (Anywhere but China), ABD (Anything but Dollar) and AI. 2020s annualized returns: 10-year UST -4%, China stocks (HSCEI) -5%, gold 15%, Nasdaq 17%.

BofA says populist electorates keep allocators ABB and in structural yield curve steepeners. Higher yields now hurt the AI stock bull as bond markets police hyperscaler capex ($240bn in '24 to $1.2tn in '27E) and free cash flow ($240bn in '24 to -$180bn in '27E).
BofA expects YCC/QE threat to cap bond yields, but says risk assets and AI need lower yields. The release valve in H1'27 is likely geopolitical peace, a big drop in oil and the end of rate hikes.

risk_factors: Job losses or a credit event could turn the tightening cycle from painful into mortal.
A disorderly rise in bond yields threatens stock market wealth and bank collateral.
Hyperscaler free cash flow turning negative (-$180bn in '27E) while capex rises to $1.2tn.
A Democratic sweep priced as risk-off, and a Democratic wave plus a jump in yields not yet priced.
China deflation becoming a global negative if lower oil fails to lift the Euro and Yen.

tension_points.bull_case: Policymakers will not allow a disorderly rise in yields, and the YCC/QE threat caps them. Tech equity flows continue (+$5.3bn, 5th week) and BofA sees a year-end rally if MAGS $70 and SMH $520 hold.
tension_points.bear_case: ABB and higher yields hurt the AI bull as bond markets police capex of $1.2tn in '27E and free cash flow of -$180bn. Hyperscaler buybacks are ending and equity issuance is rising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: MAGS below $70 or SMH below $520 before year-end.

tension_points.bull_case: China deflation is not a global problem. China financials are 2x over three years and national team buying drove $25.7bn of inflows.
tension_points.bear_case: Record-low China bond yields and a strong CNY point to China deflation as a global problem.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lower oil failing to trigger a Euro and Yen bounce would signal China deflation is a new global negative.
